claim: Within the frozen core semantics, declared finite environment model, exploration bounds, and one backend observation contract, the implemented OVLA interpreter and checker conform to the reference semantics and distinguish behaviorally equivalent from divergent IR-code executions for completed explored histories.
why_it_matters: This is the empirical support path for the dominant behavioral-verification claim C1 together with C2, C3, and C4 implementation fidelity.
minimum_convincing_evidence: E1 must show zero discrepancies against an independent semantics-derived oracle over the frozen boundary suite and completed small models; E3 must report false accepts, false rejects, completion, and uncertainty on independently constructed positive and negative cases.
anti_claim: A checker that agrees only with itself, detects only IR-derived mutants, or silently treats incomplete searches as passes is adequate evidence.
falsifier: Any unresolved semantic discrepancy, false accept on a completed exact gold case, false reject on a completed exact positive case, oracle leakage, or pass verdict with an incomplete frontier falsifies the strong form.
decision_rule: Assert only after preregistered E1 and E3 both pass and an independent results audit finds no same-scope negative evidence; otherwise narrow to the tested construct/fault classes or report a limitation.
loss_contract: Retain every generated case and run outcome: pass, semantic mismatch, false accept, false reject, adapter error, invalid input, skip, null, retry, timeout, and incomplete frontier.
falsification_test: Freeze semantics, generators, exact positive/negative labels, normalization, and thresholds before confirmatory execution; rerun from immutable snapshots and search specifically for the first counterexample.
selection_history: No new-OVLA outcomes were inspected; the blocks and thresholds were selected from the approved claims, predecessor objections, and PerCom evidence expectations on 2026-09-04.
predecessor_failures: Prior reviews questioned boundedness, compiler assumptions, generalization, and whether the old evaluation justified the claimed verifier.

claim: The frozen Timeline IR represents a predeclared reactive-temporal IoT behavior space with exact, partial, and unsupported cases reported, and the exact Explorer's completed capacity frontier is characterized as state, event, timer, rule, and horizon complexity vary.
why_it_matters: This binds C2 expressive adequacy and C4 practical boundedness to evidence without claiming universal natural-language coverage or unbounded scalability.
minimum_convincing_evidence: E2 applies a frozen taxonomy to legacy and independently sourced automations plus unsupported controls with independent annotation; E4 uses a preregistered factorial generator and real-workload anchors with complete time, memory, state, transition, and timeout accounting.
anti_claim: A hand-selected representable corpus or only median runtime is sufficient to support coverage and practical exploration claims.
falsifier: Unresolved taxonomy disagreement, systematic unsupported core categories, post-outcome corpus exclusion, missing failure outcomes, or failure to characterize the declared frontier prevents the combined claim.
decision_rule: State only category-specific adequacy and measured capacity ranges supported by completed E2/E4 strata; never extrapolate beyond the corpus, finite model, hardware, or horizon.
loss_contract: Retain exact, partial, unsupported, annotation-disagreement, invalid, skipped, failed, retried, timed-out, and resource-incomplete outcomes with denominators.
falsification_test: Freeze behavior taxonomy, corpus inclusion, negative controls, generator factors, hardware, timeout, and reporting rules before confirmatory scoring or scaling runs.
selection_history: No new-OVLA outcomes were inspected; E2 and E4 are the expressiveness and scalability axes already fixed in the controlling plan.
predecessor_failures: Prior reviews questioned single-DSL generality, limited coverage, and whether bounded execution supported broad verification language.
